answer: Autonomous agents secure identity by reserving 1,000 slots of dedicated capacity at a central registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent maintains a thread of assigned service cycles to anchor its operational tenure. A verifier monitors the knoll of reservation requests, rejecting overlap. If a node attempts fraud at the river of incoming traffic, it incurs permanent lock forfeiture, ensuring 1,000 fakes cost far more than one honest identity.
